title: Collective phase modes in twisted $d$-wave superconducting bilayers
authors: Yin Shi, Mengxian Zhao, Fei Yang, Miao Liu, Sheng Meng
abstract: Twisted cuprate bilayers have been predicted to host high-temperature chiral $d+id'$ superconductivity, originating from higher-order Josephson coupling processes. In such two-dimensional superconducting systems, long-wavelength fluctuations in the phase of the superconducting order parameter constitute gapless collective modes and therefore remain significant even at zero temperature. Here, we perform a theoretical analysis of the low-energy phase fluctuations in twisted $d$-wave superconducting bilayers, systematically retaining Josephson coupling to all orders. We demonstrate that higher-order Josephson coupling processes lead to nontrivial modifications of the phase dynamics. In particular, the stiffness of the relative phase between the two layers is finite even in the normal state, which is a direct consequence of the intralayer U(1) symmetry breaking explicitly induced by interlayer tunneling. Phase fluctuations suppress the relative-phase stiffness but enhance the overall-phase stiffness in the $d+id'$ phase. Furthermore, the relative-phase fluctuations acquire a small but finite excitation gap, which is no longer equal to the Josephson plasma frequency and is strongly suppressed upon approaching the chiral quantum critical point, indicating the breakdown of Josephson phase locking within the superconducting state.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how low-energy phase fluctuations affect superconductivity in twisted d-wave bilayers, which are candidates for high-Tc chiral superconductors. By including all orders of Josephson coupling, the authors show that these fluctuations modify the stiffnesses of superconducting phases and induce a gap in the relative-phase mode. This indicates a breakdown of Josephson phase locking near quantum critical points.
main_problem: The study analyzes low-energy phase fluctuations in twisted d-wave superconducting bilayers, which are predicted to host high-temperature chiral superconductivity.
main_result: Phase fluctuations significantly modify the collective mode dynamics, suppressing relative-phase stiffness but enhancing overall-phase stiffness in the $d+id'$ phase. The relative-phase mode acquires a gap that vanishes near the quantum critical point.
method: The authors employ a theoretical analysis using an effective action approach, systematically retaining Josephson coupling to all orders and expanding fluctuations to quadratic order.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as twisted cuprate bilayers exhibiting $d$-wave superconductivity, starting from a continuum microscopic model including interlayer tunneling and long-range Coulomb repulsion.
key_observables: Superfluid stiffnesses ($D_0, D_\pi$), the relative-phase excitation gap ($\Delta_J$), and the overall phase stiffness ($D_0$).
important_parameters: Twist angle, temperature (low T regime), interlayer tunneling amplitude ($t$), and superconducting order parameters ($\Delta_l$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to low-energy, long-wavelength fluctuations, and the derivation relies on expanding fluctuation terms up to quadratic order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate minimal superconducting gaps in the twist-angle–temperature plane, superfluid stiffnesses vs. temperature/twist angle, and Josephson gap dependence on parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving an effective action for phase fluctuations by integrating out fermionic fields to calculating specific observables like stiffnesses and gaps using mean-field theory corrections.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of collective modes and the role of higher-order couplings in determining superconducting stability is highly relevant to understanding pairing mechanisms and quantum critical points in strongly correlated superconductors.
